nodes.label: From Lookup to Reasoning (OSRE 2026 Fellowship Project)
nodes.rationale: A self-hosted RAG chatbot for Chameleon Cloud docs, an allocation-aware CHI@Edge resource advisor seamed into it, and an executable-checker benchmark that evaluates the whole system.
nodes.norm_label: from lookup to reasoning (osre 2026 fellowship project)

nodes.label: Advisor Grounding Corpus (grounding/)
nodes.rationale: One folder of Trovi-artifact docs per supported workload; resolved by the advisor as a sibling of chi-edge-advisor/.

nodes.label: FAISS + BGE Retrieval Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Questions embedded with BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5, matched against child chunks in FAISS, drawn from a per-source-type balanced pool, re-ranked by a cross-encoder; answers generated by Meta-Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct strictly from retrieved context.

nodes.label: Parent-Child Chunking
nodes.rationale: Small (~400 char) child chunks give retrieval precision; large (~2000 char) parent chunks give the model coherent context. Child chunks are prefixed with a [source_type: page title] header so embeddings capture document-level context.

nodes.label: Cross-Encoder Reranking (BAAI/bge-reranker-base)
nodes.rationale: Replaced MMR-only retrieval; reranks a per-type balanced candidate pool by (query, chunk) relevance and discards chunks below a minimum score.

nodes.label: Tiered Context Assembly (PRIMARY vs SUPPLEMENTARY)
nodes.rationale: Official docs (readthedocs + python-chi) go in a PRIMARY DOCUMENTATION section, blog/forum in SUPPLEMENTARY CONTEXT; the LLM is instructed to ground answers in primary documentation first and use supplementary content only for examples and gap-filling.

nodes.label: Two-Store Architecture (planned)
nodes.rationale: Split the FAISS index into a primary store (readthedocs, python-chi) and a supplemental store (curated blog posts, Trovi) to eliminate heuristic source-type balancing and give cleaner control over what the model treats as authoritative; would also make forum/GitBook sources safe to re-include.

nodes.label: Chameleon API MCP Server (planned live-data integration)
nodes.rationale: A Model Context Protocol server wrapping Chameleon REST APIs (Blazar reservations, node availability, hardware discovery) to answer dynamic questions; architecturally distinct from RAG — tool use rather than document retrieval — and requires designing an authentication flow.
nodes.norm_label: chameleon api mcp server (planned live-data integration)

nodes.label: Feedback & Session Logging (session_log.jsonl + feedback.db)
nodes.rationale: Every query/answer appended to session_log.jsonl; thumbs-up/down ratings with failure categories stored in SQLite feedback.db, summarised by feedback_report.py. These are the primary signals that the index is stale.

nodes.label: Two-Phase Fetch-then-Embed Index Build
nodes.rationale: Each source is fetched independently and checkpointed to _fetch_cache/ before anything is embedded, so a single source failure does not abort the run; the new index is built in a temp directory and atomically swapped into place only after the full build succeeds.

nodes.label: RAG Eval Pipeline (golden question set, eval/)
nodes.rationale: Golden question set scored via run_pipeline.py and score.py; scoring uses retrieval diagnostics (formerly cosine similarity of BGE embeddings) appended to CSV for cross-run comparison.
nodes.norm_label: rag eval pipeline (golden question set, eval/)

nodes.label: Two-Store Architecture (roadmap priority 1)
nodes.rationale: Search primary and supplemental stores independently, combine candidates, rerank together — eliminates numerical dominance of blog chunks over docs chunks. Supplemental curation criterion: only content the docs don't cover or that demonstrates a documented concept in action, never re-explanations (which introduce outdated/inconsistent information).

nodes.label: Reranker Score Threshold (0.5 cutoff)
nodes.rationale: Chunks scoring below 0.5 are excluded from context so the model says 'I don't know' rather than confabulating from weak matches.

nodes.label: Query Expansion / HyDE (planned)
nodes.rationale: Embed a hypothetical answer instead of the raw question to improve recall for vocabulary-mismatched queries (e.g. 'Error 403 Forbidden' vs the docs' 'source your openrc file').

nodes.label: H0/H1 Group Instrument (mechanism/specifics/safety)
nodes.rationale: Every check is tagged mechanism/specifics/safety and pass rates are reported per group per condition. Under held-out feeding, H1 (transfer) predicts mechanism checks pass while specifics fail; H0 (task-specific lookup) predicts both fail.

nodes.label: SWE-bench-Style Gold Admission Gate
nodes.rationale: A gold answer is admitted only after passing 100% of its own checkers — ground truth that cannot pass its own test is not ground truth. 50/50 golds pass; a 10-item negative-control suite proves the checks actually fire.

nodes.label: Computed Difficulty Tiers (key-token coverage)
nodes.rationale: tier_assign.py computes the tier of every (item, fed_set) pair from key-token coverage of the fed grounding files — tiers are measured, never asserted, inoculating against the 'hand-picked difficulty labels' critique. Only CHI@Edge-specific load-bearing, generation-agnostic tokens count.

nodes.label: Verification Levels V0/V1/V2
nodes.rationale: V0 (46 items) static AST checking only; V1 (AV01-AV04) additionally executed against a Blazar snapshot via harness/stub_chi with stdout compared to expectations; V2 (live testbed execution) dropped this cycle by decision of the fellow — no lease is ever created, no testbed quota consumed, evaluation stays reproducible offline.

nodes.label: Synthetic Blazar Snapshot
nodes.rationale: The shipped snapshot is synthetic and flagged in-file; it unblocks V1 harness development without pretending to have live data, but must be replaced by a recorded Blazar snapshot from the advisor's replay harness before reporting availability numbers.

nodes.label: Fed Grounding Files (A1-A6 flattened artifacts as run context)
nodes.rationale: grounding/ holds A1-A6 flattened artifact grounding files fed as context in matched/heldout/uncovered runs; extractions/ holds the structured Opus grep-verified extractions serving as gold provenance.
nodes.norm_label: fed grounding files (a1-a6 flattened artifacts as run context)

nodes.label: Checker-vs-Human Calibration (Cohen's kappa on v3 cells)
nodes.rationale: After code-fence recovery, agreement at human==2 rose 0.536 -> 0.893 and kappa 0.000 -> 0.783 (substantial agreement). Errors are one-directional the safe way: the checker essentially never rubber-stamps a bad answer; it models 'correct', not 'partially useful'.
nodes.norm_label: checker-vs-human calibration (cohen's kappa on v3 cells)

nodes.label: Code-Fence Recovery (--wrap-code, ast.parse gate)
nodes.rationale: Excel paste stripped all code fences (0/84 kept), making kappa 0. Recovery is opt-in and self-validating: a candidate block is fenced only if it ast.parse()s as Python, so prose and bash/dockerfile blocks are left alone — no false code. Glued labels like 'pythonimport' are un-glued only on keyword/domain-root boundaries.

nodes.label: Checker Gaps P03/P08 (actionable false negatives)
nodes.rationale: P03 expects a machine_type/machine_name kwarg but accepted answers used add_device_reservation(devices=[...]); P08's execute/output capture tokens are under-specified. Fixing both would likely lift kappa(==2) toward ~0.85-0.9 but requires editing off-limits harness/checks.py.

nodes.label: Generation-Equivalence Grading (D01)
nodes.rationale: Gold specs are authored in the OO python-chi generation (lease.Lease / container.Container); imperative answers earn full credit iff trap-free including platform_version=2 on create_container — matches what current docs push and what the advisor emits while keeping grading fair to both generations.

nodes.label: Hallucination Canaries (D09, T4b abstention items)
nodes.rationale: T4b items carry forbidden strings / profile-allowlist checks (e.g. a device_profiles entry outside {pi_libcamera, pi_sensehat, pi_gpio} fails specifics). Canaries are placed only where the fake string is certainly fake — punishing confident fabrication without punishing possibly-correct answers.

nodes.label: AST-Only Forbidden-Call Checks (D10)
nodes.rationale: Forbidden-call checks are AST-level (calls actually made), never text-level, and required/forbidden string checks run only inside extracted code blocks — a model saying 'do NOT use add_node_reservation' in prose must not be penalized for mentioning it.

nodes.label: Distractor Robustness via A4 (D08)
nodes.rationale: Only A4's start_edge_llm.ipynb content is gold-eligible; its KVM@TACC server notebooks stay in the grounding file deliberately as bare-metal distractor content — feeding A4 measures whether the model drifts to server.Server when edge is asked for.

nodes.label: Tree vs Flat Routing Result (flat 86.7% > tree 68.9% at artifact level)
nodes.rationale: Over 45 covered items (hashing-fallback embedder, L1 top-k=2, L2 top-k=3): tree hits 100% at site, 73.3% at use-case, 68.9% at artifact/chunk; flat hits 86.7% at artifact/chunk. Uncovered items (A4 bare-metal distractor targets, empty targets) are listed but not scored.
nodes.norm_label: tree vs flat routing result (flat 86.7% > tree 68.9% at artifact level)

nodes.label: chi-edge-advisor
nodes.rationale: Allocation-aware resource advisor for CHI@Edge. Intentionally mirrors the RAG-docs-chameleon stack (FAISS, BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5, OpenAI-compatible client to Tejas/Llama) so it can later be wrapped as an MCP server plugged into the chatbot. Probe, offline pipeline, and tests deliberately run stdlib-only; backend selection and API keys are never hardcoded, everything routes through advisor/config.py.

nodes.label: READ-RETRIEVE-REASON-VALIDATE-EMIT pipeline
nodes.rationale: Five function-shaped stages with append-only JSONL logging per stage so runs can be graded later; the stage shape was chosen so each stage can become an MCP tool (read_availability, retrieve_artifacts, reason, validate, emit).

nodes.label: probe_availability.py availability probe
nodes.rationale: First deliverable by design: empirically answers whether the Chameleon reference API reflects live reservation state. Verdict STATIC-ONLY — the reference API exposes zero CHI@Edge clusters/devices and no reservation fields, so both live availability and the edge hardware catalog must come from Blazar via python-chi.

nodes.label: BlazarBackend
nodes.rationale: Live availability backend via python-chi; AVAILABILITY_BACKEND=blazar is the required setting for real use because the reference API has no live state.

nodes.label: ReferenceApiBackend
nodes.rationale: Kept behind the same AvailabilityBackend interface as a static identity source; the backend is a config switch so nothing downstream cares which backend supplies live state, and no rewrite is needed if a live reference-API endpoint ever appears.

nodes.label: CHI@Edge trap validation checks
nodes.rationale: Pass/fail checks for the known CHI@Edge gotchas: architecture mismatch (arm64 vs x86_64), device actually free in the window, machine_type/device_profile exist in inventory, platform_version present, runtime=nvidia when a GPU workload lands on a Jetson.

nodes.label: python-chi spec emitter
nodes.rationale: Renders add_device_reservation + container.Container — not add_node_reservation/create_server, the two most common CHI@Edge API mistakes — and dry-checks the spec by constructing objects without submitting.

nodes.label: Production (real-stack) dependencies
nodes.rationale: None of these are required for the probe, offline pipeline, or tests (stdlib-only paths); installed only to enable real embeddings/FAISS, the LLM clients (openai->Tejas, anthropic fallback), and the live Blazar backend. Retrieval/embedding deps deliberately mirror ChameleonCloud/RAG-docs-chameleon.

nodes.label: Development dependencies (pytest)
nodes.rationale: Dev-only tooling; the suite also runs under stdlib unittest without any of these installed.

nodes.label: House-and-room integration architecture
nodes.rationale: The chatbot is the house, the advisor a room that lights up only for edge-hardware questions. In-process library chosen over a separate microservice (extra moving part to deploy and break) and over MCP model-invoked tools (the chatbot has no tool-calling layer; adding one is a big change). Everything sits behind a single ADVISOR_ENABLED switch so the original chatbot survives untouched.

nodes.label: RAG-docs-chameleon chatbot
nodes.rationale: Streamlit retrieve-then-generate app over Chameleon documentation: FAISS doc index + bge embeddings + reranker, PRIMARY/SUPPLEMENTARY context assembly, answer via a local LLM with source links.

nodes.label: advisor_room.py wrapper
nodes.rationale: Exposes exactly the two things the chatbot needs — should_fire(question) and advise(question) — making the seam literally one Python import.

nodes.label: should_fire edge-question gate
nodes.rationale: Cheap check on every question that requires BOTH an edge cue word AND a router topic score above threshold, so general documentation questions never wake the room. Added after a general SSH/floating-IP question scored identically (2.25) to the edge-SSH artifact — a deliberate precision-over-recall trade.

nodes.label: EDGE RESOURCE ADVISORY context injection
nodes.rationale: The advisor's recommendation is appended to the chatbot context under a labelled '=== EDGE RESOURCE ADVISORY ===' header matching the existing PRIMARY/SUPPLEMENTARY idiom, so the LLM treats it as one more trusted context section and produces a single unified, source-grounded answer.

nodes.label: Shared BAAI/bge-large-en-v1.5 embedding space
nodes.rationale: Both systems embed text with the same model, so the advisor's notion of relevance lives in the same mathematical space as the chatbot's and gate scores are meaningful; asserted at startup — fails loudly if the advisor ever falls back to a different embedder.

nodes.label: Local LLM brain (Ollama Qwen2.5-32B)
nodes.rationale: After losing access to hosted Llama-3.3-70B, one self-hosted Qwen2.5-32B on the 2x P100 node serves both the chatbot's answering step and the advisor's reasoning step through one shared OpenAI-style endpoint — one brain for house and room; embeddings and reranker stay on CPU to leave GPU memory for the LLM.

nodes.label: run_bench.py benchmark runner
nodes.rationale: Scripted benchmark runs against the fork and API models; run-prompts generated per item x condition (blind gets the prompt verbatim; matched/heldout/uncovered wrap grounding files in REFERENCE MATERIAL markers).

nodes.label: Scorer layout contract
nodes.rationale: runs/<condition>/<system>/<ITEM>.md with exactly three path levels — the validate_golds.ipynb recalc cell hard-requires it. Preserve code fences verbatim (the 50 hand-pasted answers lost fences on copy, causing the kappa~0 calibration problem); non-.md sidecars are invisible to the scorer; never overwrite non-empty saved responses (0-byte scaffolds may be filled).

nodes.label: Fork adapter (headless in-process pipeline)
nodes.rationale: web_rag.py cannot be imported headless (module-top-level Streamlit, st.stop() without vect_store), so the answer pipeline is composed from pure parts — rag.py load/build functions plus advisor_room — exactly as the m2_smoke.py and eval_m4.py half-precedents do. Runs condition blind because the fork does its own retrieval; feeding it reference material would double-feed.

nodes.label: manifest.json provenance record
nodes.rationale: Per-run record of adapter, system, condition, model+params, timestamps, host, per-item statuses, and sha256 content hashes of the item bank, benchmark grounding, advisor grounding corpus, and snapshot. Content hashes stand in for git SHAs because the parent repo has no commits; the fork's HEAD ab01b54 carries a dirty-diff hash for the uncommitted advisor integration.

nodes.label: anthropic/openai API adapters (dry-run only)
nodes.rationale: Model strings and params pinned in bench_config.yaml with exponential-backoff retries, but code-only for now: no API keys configured, never executed against the paid APIs, only --dry-run exercised — user decision, zero spend. A production-stub adapter name is reserved and refuses to run.

nodes.label: RetrievalRouter (flat)
nodes.rationale: Artifact classification is lexical tag/title token scoring, not embedding-based — embedding similarity only enters later at chunk ranking inside store.search(). Selection keeps artifacts strictly above the relevance floor with fallback to the single best; budget is split proportional to classify score with rounding drift trimmed so budgets sum exactly (test-pinned). Provenance is an ordered de-duplicated artifact_id list feeding Recommendation.grounded_by.

nodes.label: RouterTree (site -> use-case -> artifact)
nodes.rationale: Level-0 hard site gate fires only when WorkloadSpec.site is set, so plain-string traffic (CLI, advisor_room) can never be gated; Level-1 soft use-case top-k routing; Level-2 reuses the flat router's _select/_budget/_finish code. Byte-identical to the flat router with one populated branch and default knobs (pinned by test_byte_identical_single_branch); divergence only via the explicit use_case_top_k ablation knob. Adds per-section SectionProvenance without altering legacy provenance.

nodes.label: Flat store + allow-set post-filter
nodes.rationale: Key finding: the FAISS IndexFlatIP is built and then never queried — search is a pure-Python brute-force cosine with an artifact_id allow-set post-filter. At 5 artifacts / low hundreds of chunks this is exact, simple, and microseconds-cheap, so two-level logical partitioning reduces to deriving a richer allow-set plus a dozen-vector partition-descriptor table; per-partition FAISS indexes or metadata filtering (which IndexFlatIP lacks anyway) would be pure ceremony.

nodes.label: Table A7 tree-vs-flat ablation
nodes.rationale: ablate_router.py runs every benchmark item through both routers scoring target-artifact hits per level. At non-restrictive --l1-k 3 the tree's L2/chunk hit-rates (86.7%) exactly equal flat's — byte-identical parity holds on real prompts; truncating to top-2 use-cases costs ~18 points of artifact recall, quantifying the routing-aggressiveness trade-off. 45/50 items covered (A4 bare-metal distractors and designed no-source items excluded); deterministic HashingEmbedder default for reproducibility.

nodes.label: Prototype state snapshot (2026-07-01)
nodes.rationale: Shared-context build notes so anyone picking up the prototype understands what was built, why, what failed, and what remains without reconstructing chat logs. Records the verified end-to-end run (run_id b359ccd80d0b): 63 live devices via Blazar, edge-picamera-image selected, all six validator checks PASS, runnable spec emitted — closing the Milestone 1 'action gap' failure.

nodes.label: Blazar authentication journey (six pitfalls)
nodes.rationale: python-chi imports blazarclient without declaring it; upstream python-blazarclient lacks the Chameleon fork's .device resource; OIDC SSO tokens fail non-interactively so Application Credentials are required; stale OS_* vars contaminate sessions; app credentials embed project scope so chi.set('project_name') triggers HTTP 401 (guarded in blazar.py); Device objects expose device_type/supported_device_profiles, and hardware.get_devices() must be used instead of raw blazarclient list() which reports type=container for everything.

nodes.label: GOAL execution plan (M0-M4)
nodes.rationale: Self-contained autonomous execution plan with hard acceptance gates and stop-and-ask points. Locked decisions: Ollama/GGUF because Pascal P100s lack tensor cores and AWQ/Marlin/FlashAttn kernels (vLLM+AWQ dead end); Qwen2.5-14B Q4 default with a 32B option if 2x P100; embeddings/reranker stay on CPU to reserve VRAM; reference_api backend to skip CHI creds; in-process import dissolves the MCP and tool-calling blockers; gate reuses router.classify so no new classifier and no wasted LLM call; rag.py diff must stay upstream-contributable.

nodes.label: Execution running log (M0-M4 gates)
nodes.rationale: All gates passed with observed evidence on hardware: 2x Tesla P100 found so the user chose Qwen2.5-32B over the locked 14B default; Ollama 0.32's CUDA-13 runtime silently fell back to CPU on driver 560, fixed by pinning 0.11.11; M4 eval docs 8/8 and edge 4/4; an SSH/floating-IP false positive was fixed with the should_fire edge-cue guard; deployment hardened to a systemd rag-app service after bare streamlit died on SSH teardown.

nodes.label: web_rag.py 459-468 injection seam
nodes.rationale: The model only ever sees one opaque context string built by build_context() and passed to chain.invoke(), so anything appended between those two calls reaches the model with zero prompt-template changes — the natural place to run the advisor and merge its output as a third labelled section. The chatbot has no tool/agent/MCP layer at all (grep-verified), which pushed the design toward context-string injection.

nodes.label: Two-store FAISS compatibility verdict
nodes.rationale: Same bge model and normalization mean cross-store scores are numerically comparable, but the index containers (LangChain save_local vs raw IndexFlatIP + JSON), metadata schemas (parent_id/source_type vs artifact_id/chunk_index), chunking (parent/child 2000/400 vs single-level 1200), and partition models all differ — keep two stores and federate at retrieval time; merging indices would destroy the advisor's artifact_id partitioning, its core value.

nodes.label: HashingEmbedder offline-fallback footgun
nodes.rationale: The advisor silently selects a hashing embedder when ADVISOR_OFFLINE is set or sentence-transformers/torch is missing; those vectors are not in bge space, so any federated retrieval or gate scoring must assert the bge path or cross-store scores are garbage — flagged as a real footgun before integration.

nodes.label: Runbook (relaunch + gotchas)
nodes.rationale: How to relaunch the stack on the Chameleon P100 node: systemd rag-app service, Ollama model check, one-time index build, port 8501 security-group note, and the gotchas that cost hours (Ollama pin, stray advisor .env, Docker-baked FEEDBACK_DB_PATH default crashing under systemd).

nodes.label: Ollama <=0.11.x version pin gotcha
nodes.rationale: Ollama 0.32 bundles a CUDA-13 runtime requiring NVIDIA driver >=570; the node has 560, so it silently runs the model on CPU (~2.4 tok/s, GPUs idle). Ollama 0.11.11 ships a CUDA v12 runtime that uses the P100s (~9 tok/s). Pin until the driver is upgraded to 570+.

nodes.label: Stray advisor .env override gotcha
nodes.rationale: The advisor's config loads its own package .env first; a stray ~/chi-edge-advisor/.env on the node overrode the LLM provider/model and forced heuristic-only fallback. The RAG .env is the single source of truth — keep the advisor's deleted and exclude .env when rsyncing.

nodes.label: rag-app systemd service
nodes.rationale: A bare streamlit run launched over SSH dies on session teardown; the systemd unit with Restart=always keeps the app persistent and auto-restarting.

nodes.label: Testing guide
nodes.rationale: How to exercise the running system: health check, SSH-tunnel vs open-port UI access, dormant-vs-fire functional tests, standalone-mode test, and result nuances — cold-start reload, double-call latency on edge turns, 9 tok/s P100 ceiling, produced_by=tejas vs heuristic, conservative cue-word gate, grounded-only answers by design.

nodes.label: eval_m4.py automated eval
nodes.rationale: Runs the gate + advisor over 8 docs + 4 edge questions without the UI. docs=8/8 means no general question falsely fired the room; edge=4/4 means every edge question fired AND grounded in the expected artifact. produced_by=tejas means the LLM path worked ('tejas' is just the OpenAI-compat client name pointed at local Ollama); by=heuristic signals a fault, usually a stray advisor .env.

nodes.label: edge-cpu-inference artifact
nodes.rationale: teaching-on-testbeds tutorial (NSF Grant No. 2230079): CPU-based image-classification inference on a CHI@Edge device — edge inference trades raw speed for the privacy/latency/bandwidth benefits of not shipping input data to the cloud.

nodes.label: CPU inference notebook (MobileNet TFLite)
nodes.author: Deepak Chaurasiya
nodes.rationale: Launches a python:3.9-slim container (port 22, platform_version=2) on an existing CHI@Edge lease, sets up SSH, uploads image_model, and runs a quantized MobileNet via tflite-runtime. MobileNet's cheap convolutions and quantization are chosen specifically to cut edge inference time when no hardware acceleration is available.

nodes.label: Chen & Ran (2019) Deep Learning With Edge Computing: A Review
nodes.author: Deepak Chaurasiya
nodes.norm_label: chen & ran (2019) deep learning with edge computing: a review

nodes.label: Edge device reservation notebook (reserve.md)
nodes.author: Deepak Chaurasiya
nodes.rationale: Reserves a raspberrypi4-64 on CHI@Edge via lease.add_device_reservation with a 10-hour lease_duration, plus a standalone deletion section.

nodes.label: edge-picamera-image artifact
nodes.rationale: Pi Camera Module 3 showcase: iot-rpi4-picam* device (device_type raspberrypi4-64) + pi_libcamera profile + image ghcr.io/chameleoncloud/edge-picamera-image:latest; captures stills via rpicam-still and the picamera2 library and H264 video via rpicam-vid; object-oriented python-chi style.

nodes.label: pi_libcamera device profile
nodes.rationale: Exposes the /dev nodes (dma_heap, media*, v4l-subdev0, vchiq, vcsm-cma, video*) and read-only /run/udev that the libcamera stack needs inside the container.

nodes.label: Pi Camera tutorial notebook
nodes.rationale: End-to-end flow: choose site/project, filter iot-rpi4-picam* devices, 3-hour lease, launch container with pi_libcamera, rpicam-hello check, still capture (CLI + picamera2 helper camera_test.py), video capture, cleanup. Source quirks (video1.mp4 vs video1.h264, 30fps text vs --framerate 24) preserved verbatim.

nodes.label: edge_sensehat_image artifact
nodes.rationale: One container image (ghcr.io/chameleoncloud/edge_sensehat_image:latest) serves two sense-hat boards: Part A RPi Sense HAT via the sense_hat library + pi_sensehat profile on iot-rpi4-picam3; Part B Waveshare Sense HAT (B) via Adafruit CircuitPython + pi_gpio profile on iot-rpi-cm4-02, with Blinka env-var workarounds (RPI_LGPIO_REVISION, BLINKA_FORCECHIP/FORCEBOARD) for the missing /sys/firmware/devicetree inside containers.

nodes.label: pi_sensehat device profile
nodes.rationale: Exposes i2c, gpiomem, gpiochip, framebuffer /dev/fb0, and /dev/input event devices for the RPi Sense HAT.

nodes.label: pi_gpio device profile
nodes.rationale: Exposes i2c, gpiomem, and gpiochip devices for GPIO/I2C access (Waveshare Sense HAT path).

nodes.label: Sense HAT tutorial notebook (Parts A+B)
nodes.rationale: Merged from rpi_sense.ipynb and waveshare_sense.ipynb (only the duplicated auth cell trimmed). Shared auth -> 4-hour device lease -> launch container with the part's profile/env -> read sensors (i2cdetect, sense_hat library or Adafruit CircuitPython /examples scripts) -> cleanup. Source inconsistencies (soufianejounaid image name vs ghcr.io code, revision 0xd03115 text vs 0xd03140 code) preserved verbatim.

nodes.label: edge_ssh_image artifact
nodes.rationale: SSH-enabled Ubuntu 22.04 container on CHI@Edge: image ghcr.io/chameleoncloud/edge_ssh_image:latest, exposed port 22, RSA key injection into authorized_keys, floating IP association. Uses the functional python-chi style (create_lease/create_container), unlike the other artifacts' object-oriented style; count=2 reserves two devices but only one is used — preserved verbatim.

nodes.label: SSH on CHI@Edge tutorial notebook
nodes.rationale: 1-day raspberrypi4-64 lease -> SSH container on port 22 (workdir /home, platform_version=2) -> upload public key, chmod 600, append to authorized_keys -> associate floating IP -> print ssh root@<ip> -> destroy container.

nodes.label: serve-edge-chi artifact
nodes.rationale: teaching-on-testbeds tutorial (NSF Grant No. 2230079): benchmark baseline vs INT8-quantized ONNX models with onnxruntime (CPUExecutionProvider) on a Raspberry Pi 5 (Arm Cortex-A76) at CHI@Edge — the edge leg of the GourmetGram model-serving options (<15ms median latency, <5MB model). Lease is made via the Horizon GUI against named nyu-rpi5-XX devices; the container is a quay.io jupyter/minimal-notebook launched with python-chi. Added to the advisor grounding corpus as benchmark artifact A5.

nodes.label: RAG model parameter sweep (Models 1-14 + baselines)
nodes.rationale: Table of 14 RAG configurations sweeping chunk_size/chunk_overlap, k/fetch_k, MMR, documentation-source breadth (index-pages-only vs full), prompt technique (Simple -> Enhanced -> Enhanced+Evaluator), bge-reranker-large re-ranking, and a dual-LLM evaluator design; embedding model shifts from bge-large-en to bge-base-en-v1.5 for reranked models; LLM is Llama3.1 throughout. Baselines: GPT-5 with internet search and Llama 3.1 without RAG.

nodes.label: Simple Prompt
nodes.rationale: Short system prompt: answer from the provided context with source links, say 'I don't know' when the answer is not clearly in context, keep answers to a maximum of 5 sentences.

nodes.label: Enhanced Prompt
nodes.rationale: Structured ROLE/TASK/INSTRUCTIONS/OUTPUT-FORMAT prompt: interpret user intent, synthesize across ALL context sources rather than listing them, mandatory 'I don't know' when absent from context, no outside knowledge, and a structured 'Read More' citation list with titles and URLs.

nodes.label: Evaluator Prompt (dual-LLM design)
nodes.rationale: A second LLM acts as expert editor/grader over the first draft: removes unsupported (hallucinated) content, integrates missed context, enforces synthesis, replaces ungrounded answers with 'I don't know', and corrects the Read More citation list — outputting only the refined answer.

hyperedges.label: CHI@Edge Trovi Artifact Corpus A1-A6 (extractions + grounding)
